report:
I cannot identify a single, specific objective or domain from this evidence.

What I do see: the difference is dominated by a BOS/position-0–like global offset across layers, and the logit-lens tokens in later layers repeatedly lean toward heterogeneous but “serious” real‑world vocabulary—legal (“law,” “wrong/incorrect”), medical (“surgeon,” “clinic,” “surgery”), disaster/negativity (“tragic/tragedy,” “rescue”), sports proper nouns (“Royals,” “Manny,” “baseman”), and some directive/compliance phrasing (“Do/Check/ensure/adhere/proactive”). This could suggest a mild tilt toward a formal/newswire or compliance-advisory register, but the signal is mixed and lacks clear hallmark markers (e.g., no consistent “said/according to,” or refusal/safety phrases). Patchscope readouts are missing, so there’s no corroborating behavioral continuation. Overall, the evidence doesn’t cleanly support naming a specific objective or domain difference.
